clue.text: Tennis player's light stroke caught previous Wimbledon champ out finally

parts.note: a pat is a light tap or stroke
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the final letter of the champion's surname is put out, i.e. dropped

parts.note: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1975, before Cash's 1987 title

explanation.surface: A commentator describes a deft shot that dismissed a former Wimbledon winner at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out finally' removes the last E of ASHE, leaving ASH; the 's on 'Tennis player's' is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Cash is the Australian who won the Wimbledon men's singles title in 1987.

clue.text: Picture power shifting to pro-Socialist PM

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

indicators.note: shifting means the letters of the following words are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone describes a photo of a prime minister drifting towards left-wing politics.
explanation.walkthrough: P stays at the front; 'shifting' rearranges TO PRO-SOCIALIST PM to give the rest of the 1949 Ealing comedy title. Pimlico is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and this is a classic Ealing Studios comedy from 1949.

clue.text: See 1
Speaker's given permission audibly

indicators.note: the words that follow are as a speaker says them, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: allowed means given permission

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House has been allowed to talk out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' looks like a reference to the Commons Speaker but signals a sound-alike: ALLOWED is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something out loud means saying it so it can be heard, which is what audibly describes.

clue.text: Gangster's cover

definitions.meaning: a hoodlum or gangster, shortened slang; the 's reads as 'is'
a covering for the head attached to a coat, or a car's bonnet in the US

explanation.definitionFit: Hood is short for hoodlum, a criminal, and is also a head covering on a garment.

clue.text: Vote against opening a school run by nuns

parts.note: a con is an argument or vote against, as in pros and cons
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: An instruction to oppose the founding of a school managed by a religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like a verb (starting a school) but is the noun VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent school is one run by an order of nuns, often called simply a convent.

clue.text: Announced European traveller can get dinars .. using this?

definitions.text: Announced European traveller can get dinars .. using this?

indicators.note: announced means the word that follows is spoken, so we take its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a Czech is a European, from the Czech Republic
a car is a vehicle that travels, a traveller in a loose sense
D is the abbreviation for dinar, the currency of Serbia and several Arab states

explanation.surface: A tourist from Europe wonders whether a bank card will let them withdraw local currency abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: CZECH is said the same as CHEQUE; 'can get' and 'using this?' frame the whole clue as a description of what the card lets a traveller do.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque guarantee card once let a traveller cash cheques abroad and draw foreign money such as dinars.

clue.text: Fresh milk supplier in a state

parts.note: new means fresh
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow, named after the Channel Island

explanation.surface: Fresh milk is being provided somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh milk' reads as one phrase, but 'Fresh' gives NEW and 'milk supplier' is the cow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty United States, on the Atlantic coast beside New York.

clue.text: Number carried in freighter

indicators.note: carried in means the answer is held within the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A count of items transported on a cargo ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside fr-EIGHT-er.
explanation.definitionFit: The number one more than seven is a number, so the definition is a general class.

clue.text: Spanish fighter rushed round, having captured resistance leader

indicators.note: having captured means the first pieces hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road
O is round in shape

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word resistance

explanation.surface: A Spanish soldier dashed about after seizing the head of an insurgent movement.
explanation.walkthrough: TORE and O hold R, the leader of 'resistance', between them. 'Fighter' suggests a soldier, but it is a bullfighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a bullfighter in Spain, someone who fights bulls in the ring.

clue.text: Student protest beginning in part of London again

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the London district

parts.note: Soho is a district of London's West End

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word protest

parts.note: more means again, as in once more

explanation.surface: A student demonstration starts up again in a district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the beginning of 'protest' inside the West End district; 'Student' looks like part of the protest picture but is the definition, an American term.
explanation.definitionFit: In American colleges a second-year student is called by this name.

clue.text: Bet composer has missed out note

indicators.note: has missed out means a letter is omitted from the composer's name

parts.note: Richard Wagner was a German composer
N is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A musical gambler claims a composer skipped a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is not a musical letter here but N, the abbreviation for note in references; removing it from WAGNER leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager is a bet, money staked on an outcome.

clue.text: Sounds like something to help with unruly mop

definitions.text: Sounds like something to help with unruly mop

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of the word mop are disordered
sounds like means we take a word for its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: aid is something that helps

explanation.surface: A suggestion for taming messy hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' and 'unruly' both work on pieces, but the whole clue also describes the hair product, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented hair ointment used to keep untidy hair in place.

clue.text: Old quarters should be demolished right away, and that's official

indicators.note: demolished means the letters are knocked down and rebuilt in another order
away means the letter is taken out of the word quarters

explanation.surface: An announcement that old housing must be pulled down immediately, made officially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once' but means drop R from QUARTERS; O plus QUATERS is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaestor was a Roman magistrate in charge of public finance, an official of the state.

clue.text: Young scout finds a means to keep working

parts.note: Beavers are the youngest section of the Scout movement
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A Cub-age scout discovers a method of staying busy.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is to work hard and steadily, keeping at a task like the industrious animal.

clue.text: BBC bigwig rejected hard line

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a tier is a row or line

explanation.surface: A senior broadcasting executive refused to take a tough stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard line' reads as a firm policy, but it is H plus TIER, turned back by 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC, its founding chief.

clue.text: The pals and me, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders aloud who counts among their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link: the anagram uses THE PALS plus ME; the whole clue doubles as a description of companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpmates are companions and helpers, which pals and oneself may be to each other.

clue.text: Steps taken to present apology

definitions.meaning: a dance in which a partner may be claimed by cutting in, so steps are danced
a polite phrase said to apologise or to ask someone to move

explanation.surface: Measures adopted to deliver a formal apology.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse-me is a ballroom dance where partners can be swapped, and the phrase is a polite apology.

clue.text: Create fuss as Jenkins and Bussell might

definitions.meaning: to make an unnecessary fuss about something
Katherine Jenkins is a Welsh singer and Darcey Bussell a British ballet dancer, so one sings and one dances

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make an excessive fuss, while literally a singer and a dancer would perform these.

clue.text: See 17
Deliver a series of balls? Wow

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to bowl a set of six deliveries, called an over

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over is six balls bowled; to amaze someone is also to knock them flat.

clue.text: The whole of this country could fit into that part of Canada

indicators.note: fit into means the country's letters go inside the other word

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in yon hill
UK, the United Kingdom, is this country from a British setter's view

explanation.surface: A geographic boast that Britain would sit wholly inside a Canadian territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The whole of' is a link that also states the geographic fact; 'could fit into' puts the country inside the old word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Yukon is a territory in north-west Canada, bordering Alaska.

clue.text: Blonde bombshells, for instance: mostly dim females

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word dim, losing its last letter

parts.note: shes are females, using the pronoun as a noun

explanation.surface: A rude remark that glamorous blondes are largely unintelligent women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of 'dim'; 'Blonde bombshells' is an example, so the definition carries 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes is slang for attractive people, and a blonde bombshell is one example.

clue.text: South American artist receives me privately

indicators.note: receives means the pieces take the following word inside them

parts.note: the Inca were the people of the ancient Peruvian empire
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Peruvian painter welcomes the speaker in confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts 'me' between the two pieces; RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal hearing held in camera takes place in private, closed to the public.

clue.text: Country set?

definitions.meaning: a matching service of porcelain crockery

explanation.definitionFit: China is the Asian nation, and also porcelain tableware such as a tea set.

clue.text: Boy is in van touring northern Crete, perhaps

indicators.note: in the van means at the front, so the word is goes first
touring means the boy goes round the letter for northern

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad drives a van round the north of a Greek holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is not a vehicle but the front, as in vanguard; 'touring' wraps the boy round N for northern.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is a large Greek island in the Mediterranean, an example of the class.

clue.text: Deal with skilled manual worker, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the following is heard, so we use its sound

parts.note: C2 is the UK social grade for skilled manual workers, used in market research

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to handle a tradesman, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: In British market-research social grades, C2 means skilled manual workers; C2 said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to something is to attend to it or take care of it.

clue.text: Royal family gathering brought to an end

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: brought to an end means we take only the end letter of the word gathering

explanation.surface: A royal household meeting is wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought to an end' looks like a description of the gathering finishing, but it takes the last letter, G.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a royal person, and a king is the male monarch.

clue.text: Man is given time for robbery

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man is sentenced to time for a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given time' sounds like a prison term, but 'given' is a link and 'time' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, particularly a large planned one.

clue.text: Make a note of rent widow squandered

indicators.note: squandered means the letters are wasted and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A ledger entry: the rent that the widow wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squandered' rearranges RENT WIDOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down is to record it in writing, so you make a note of it.

clue.text: Russian player needs visa when visiting southern Kentucky

indicators.note: when visiting means the permit goes inside the other letters

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky
a pass is a permit such as a visa

explanation.surface: A Russian sportsman requires travel papers to enter the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when visiting' sets the permit inside the two abbreviations; 'player' is a chess player, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Spassky was a Soviet chess grandmaster and world champion, a chess player.

clue.text: Movie girl, for instance, circulates at endless wild parties

indicators.note: circulates means the letters are turned round

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for for example

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: orgies are wild parties

explanation.surface: A film starlet mingles at debauched parties that never finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulates' turns EG into GE; 'endless' trims ORGIES to ORGIE. The movie is the 1966 British film Georgy Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the 1966 film Georgy Girl, played by Lynn Redgrave, is a movie girl.
